title: NIST CSF tiers get misread in board reporting
angle: The Govern function is the part people skip, and tier ratings are routinely presented to boards as something they do not mean. Both are concrete, correctable mistakes.
keyPoints: Presenting a Tier 3 rating to a board as 'we have strong security' is misleading. Tiers describe how far cyber risk management is integrated into wider organisational risk management, not overall security capability.
An organisation can sit at Tier 4 on governance and Tier 1 on technical detection coverage at the same time.
The Govern function exists to force risk context. If the risk tolerance and risk strategy subcategories are not handled first, the rest of the framework has no direction.
It is possible to implement the framework broadly and still have no board level accountability, no documented risk appetite, and no supply chain governance beyond a line in a vendor questionnaire.
The common failure mode is treating CSF as a checklist and ticking subcategories without the risk rationale behind them.

sources.title: NIST CSF 2.0: Understanding and Implementing the Govern Function
